report: Reviewed the complete claim, both ordinary parser implementation associations and all three ordinary annotated tests; there are no TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites. Independently verified exact current-to-historical source matches for parser.rs, language.rs and value_types.rs. The historical rationale remains sufficient after reassessment: type_declaration reads and retains the name and optional parameters; compact opaque declarations require prose then a semicolon, while braced declarations require prose then an immediate closing brace. Both return TypeShape::Opaque, so neither fields nor variants can be acquired, and any payload is rejected by the closing-brace expectation. The tokenizer/prose helper requires triple quotes. opaque_types_require_prose_and_have_no_payload visibly checks both valid spellings, opaque shape, retained parameter and exact prose, and rejects missing prose in both spellings and a field payload. parses_structs_enums_and_opaque_generics corroborates generic braced opaque shape and description in a mixed declaration document. rejects_malformed_value_declarations additionally rejects a generic opaque declaration without prose. These assertions would catch accidentally optional descriptions, incorrect representation or accepting field payloads; the same immediate-close implementation excludes variants. Captured parse_body confirms its only role is wrapping the supplied declaration in a valid crate header and invoking the reviewed parser. No additional semantic helpers are needed for this claim. This is source inspection and exact baseline comparison, not new behavioral execution: I ran review start/read/record and comparison commands; no tests or build were run by me. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing sage-meta functional tests and a successful root build. No source edits or requested changes.
